newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hypo-Bank seeks to expand funds business.
newsitem.headline: Hypo-Bank seeks to expand funds business.

text.p: Germany's Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechsel Bank AG on Thursday said it was keen to expand its fund management business and would consider acquisitions to do so.

In a telephone interview, Hypo-Bank board member Martin Koelsch said the bank would use its newly acquired 65 percent majority in Foreign & Colonial Management Limited of London as a starting point to expand its funds activities.
"This was a clear strategy with Foreign & Colonial. We will be taking a look at additional acquisitions, or at least seek to expand the business," Koelsch said.
Hypo-Bank says seeks to expand funds business
Asked if imminent takeovers were likely, Koelsch said: "Who knows? You need to assess the availability and the price margins."
Hypo-Bank was not yet "in the big league" in funds management, Koelsch said, with around 94 billion marks under management, counting retail and institutional business.

"I think you would need 150 billion marks at least to be a really big player," Koelsch said, adding that Hypo-Bank was mainly keen to use its funds business to get a better balance on its fee income side, by increasing the contribution from securities business.
Hypo-Bank earlier said it expected to add between 150 and 170 million marks to its fee income through its consolidation of Foreign & Colonial.
"But that is not the last word," Koelsch remarked.
Koelsch said Hypo-Bank would not try to change the way F&C operates once it has full control of the unit.
"We have a clear understanding that the corporate governance will remain the same. This unit has a London culture which will remain," he said.
One of the benefits of taking on F & C was the chance of better co-ordinating its activities in emerging markets, especially in eastern Europe, he said.
Koelsch noted that asset management had long been one of the two main strands of business at Hypo-Bank, which is mainly known as a mortgage specialist.
